posts.title: Introduction to Blazor
posts.body: Blazor is a framework for building interactive web applications using C# and .NET. It enables developers to create single-page applications without relying on JavaScript.

posts.title: Optimizing SQL Queries
posts.body: Optimizing SQL queries is essential for improving database performance. Techniques such as indexing, query rewriting, and proper joins can significantly enhance query execution speed.

posts.title: Understanding Windows Authentication in .NET
posts.body: Windows Authentication allows applications to authenticate users based on their Windows credentials. This is commonly used in intranet applications for seamless authentication.

posts.title: C# Password Hashing with Salt
posts.body: Using salt in password hashing enhances security by preventing precomputed attacks like rainbow table attacks. A secure hashing algorithm like PBKDF2, bcrypt, or Argon2 is recommended.

posts.title: Setting Up CI/CD Pipelines in .NET
posts.body: A CI/CD pipeline automates the process of building, testing, and deploying .NET applications. Tools like GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, and Jenkins can be used to streamline deployments.

posts.title: Understanding Model Classes in C#
posts.body: In C#, a model class serves as a blueprint for representing data in an application. These classes are used to structure data, define properties, and facilitate interactions between different layers of the application, such as databases, APIs, and UI components.
